messages:
erin: I pushed a tiny sample that experiments with a different ergonomic surface for Generator streams in Go: an Iterator with Next(ctx) instead of a channel range. The goal is to make resume/handshake semantics explicit and avoid the common "reuse request ctx" footgun. Thoughts?

 taylor: link?
erin: https://git.redwood/internal/sampleapps/gen-iter-next. core idea: callers call iter.Next(ctx) per-loop, so they naturally supply a fresh ctx for each step and for resume handshakes. snippet: 
```go
it := client.Generators.Iterator(opts)
for {
  ch, err := it.Next(ctx) // ctx per call
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if errors.Is(err, ErrStreamDetached) {
    // try to reattach with a fresh ctx and idempotency token
    rctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
    resumed, rerr := it.Resume(rctx, ResumeOpts{ResumeKey: "user:123"})
    cancel()
    if rerr != nil { return rerr }
    continue
  }
  if err != nil { return err }
  handle(ch)
}
```

noah: interesting. Iterator.Next makes the ctx footgun less likely since users typically use the request ctx per iteration. But it doesn't eliminate the problem if they stash a short-lived ctx somewhere.

 taylor: how does Resume differ from the Resume we already have? iirc our Resume attaches over a single handshake and then returns a channel-based stream.
erin: proposal: Iterator.Resume(ctx, opts) is idempotent-for-client: it sends ResumeKey + last-seq to server. server should treat duplicate resumes with same key+seq as a noop (200) and incompatible attempts as 409. SDK translates 409->ErrReplayConflict. Also Resume will attempt a small handshake retry loop if it sees transient 502/503 from token-service rather than surfacing immediate ErrDeadline if ctx was unfortunate.

noah: careful: automatic handshake retry makes the caller's ctx semantics fuzzy. If Resume retries internally for ~2s, the caller may expect Resume to respect their ctx deadline. Maybe have Resume(ctx) respect ctx and a separate ResumeWithBackoff(ctx, opts) for ergonomic retries.
erin: good point. alternative: Resume(ctx) only uses ctx; Iterator.Attach(ctx) does an internal bounded backoff retry and returns an Iterator attached or an explicit ErrAttachFailed. Attach would be ergonomic for most apps and still let power users call Resume with strict ctx.

taylor: also we should expose a sentinel ErrStreamDetached from Next so callers can distinguish a server-driven detach vs regular completion. Right now we conflate with io.EOF in the Go SDK and that bit us in CI.
erin: yes, sample app demonstrates ErrStreamDetached plus it exposes it via Iterator.DetachMeta() to show server reason codes like "auth_rotate" or "node_restart" for observability.

noah: server-side needs to be idempotent on resume. Ops note: accept (resume_key,last_seq) and return 200 if compatible, 409 for conflict, 422 for unknown session. SDK maps those to ErrResumed, ErrReplayConflict, ErrUnknownSession respectively.
erin: Metrics: gen.iterator.resume_attempts, gen.iterator.resume_outcome={attached,conflict,failed} and gen.iterator.detach_reasons to track how many users hit the detach-vs-eof problem.

taylor: parity note: make sure Node and Python SDKs offer Iterator.Next(ctx)/async iter equivalent. Also add a small migration guide in devdocs explaining patterns: channel-range vs Next(ctx) and when to use Attach vs Resume.
erin: test plan in repo: three recipes - (A) naive channel reuse ctx -> shows immediate ErrDeadline in CI, (B) Iterator.Next with fresh ctx per call -> robust, (C) Attach helper that does bounded backoff -> ergonomic. Includes unit tests asserting ErrStreamDetached != io.EOF and a replay-conflict repro test.
